qs.q: The first microorganism to satisfy Koch's postulates (in the late 19th century) was Vibrio cholerae, responsible for cholera.
qs.e: Robert Koch successfully applied his postulates to demonstrate that Vibrio cholerae was the causative agent of cholera. This was a landmark achievement in microbiology and epidemiology.

ai.subject: Microbiology & immunology
ai.summary: Vibrio cholerae is a gram‑negative, curved rod that thrives in brackish water and causes profuse, rice‑water diarrhea via cholera toxin. Prompt rehydration saves lives.

sections.p: Vibrio cholerae is a motile, facultative anaerobe found in coastal and freshwater environments. It produces cholera toxin, a potent activator of intestinal cAMP, leading to massive fluid loss.
b: Gram‑negative, comma‑shaped rod
Oxidase‑positive, grows on alkaline media
Serogroups O1 and O139 cause epidemic disease

sections.p: The organism’s flagella enable rapid movement in water; its toxin is encoded by a lysogenic bacteriophage (CTXφ).
b: Flagellated, polar flagellum
Cholera toxin (CT) = AB5 exotoxin
Acid‑labile; high inoculum needed unless stomach acid is reduced

sections.p: Infection follows ingestion of contaminated water or seafood. The bacteria colonize the small‑intestine epithelium, secrete CT, and are shed in large numbers in stool.
b: Fecal‑oral route via contaminated water
Seafood (raw oysters) can concentrate organisms
Human carriers can spread disease during outbreaks

sections.p: Cholera presents with sudden onset watery diarrhea, vomiting, and dehydration; fever is usually absent. Severity is graded by dehydration and shock.
b: Profuse “rice‑water” stools (>1 L/h)
Mild: <5 % body weight loss; Moderate: 5‑10 %; Severe: >10 % or shock
Complications: hypovolemic shock, renal failure, death

sections.p: Clinical suspicion is confirmed by stool culture or rapid antigen test; in low‑resource settings, stool microscopy for motile curved rods can guide therapy.
b: Stool culture on TCBS agar shows yellow colonies
Rapid dipstick detects cholera toxin antigen
PCR for ctxA gene when available

t.b: Identifies V. cholerae and serogroup; confirms diagnosis when positive
Provides bedside confirmation; useful when culture unavailable
Detects motile curved bacilli; supportive evidence if labs limited

sections.p: Rehydration is the cornerstone; antibiotics shorten illness and reduce transmission. Public health measures focus on safe water, sanitation, and oral cholera vaccine.
b: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) first line
IV Ringer’s lactate for severe dehydration
Doxycycline or azithromycin for adults; erythromycin for children
Avoid quinolones in areas with high resistance

sections.p: Key points tested: classic stool appearance, dehydration grading, first‑line rehydration, and the role of cholera toxin in cAMP elevation.
b: Rice‑water stool = cholera
Dehydration >10 % = severe, needs IV fluids
CTX toxin acts on Gs protein → ↑cAMP

whenToSeekHelp: Severe dehydration (dry mucous membranes, sunken eyes, rapid pulse, low blood pressure)

faq.q: Why is fever usually absent in cholera?
faq.a: The toxin causes secretory diarrhea without triggering a systemic inflammatory response.
